INDEPENDENCE VS. INSTINCT
"Independence is a social product... it is illogical to try
to explain the independence of man on the basis of a
biological instinct to protect his existence."
Nature gives man a sophisticated physical
organ (the brain), but society gives him the
attributes required to dominate the world.

THE FUNDAMENTAL
PRINCIPLE
MAN IS THE MASTER
OF EVERYTHING AND
DECIDES EVERYTHING
MASTER OF EVERYTHING:
Addresses position. Man is not subordinate to the
objective world, he dominates it.
DECIDES EVERYTHING:
Addresses role. Man plays the decisive role in
transforming the world and shaping his destiny.
Juche actively rejects Metaphysics
(fatalism/predetermined destiny) and
Idealism (supernatural control), asserting
instead that man is the ultimate
transformer of the material world.

THE THREE REVOLUTIONS
(THE CONTINUOUS STRUGGLE)
Marxism largely viewed the revolution as complete
once the socialist mode of production was established
Juche argues this is only the beginning.
ESTABLISHMENT OF SOCIALIST SYSTEM
IDEOLOGICAL REVOLUTION
Continuous struggle to free the masses from outdated ideas.
TECHNOLOGICAL REVOLUTION
Continuous struggle to free the masses from the fetters of nature.
CULTURAL REVOLUTION
Continuous struggle to create sound cultural conditions.
A continuous revolution in ideology, technology, and culture is the law-governed requirement
to prevent backsliding and fully achieve independence.

THE LEADER
Will of the Collective
The culmination of Juche philosophy is the concept of 'single-hearted unity.' When man's
independence and creativity are fully subordinated to a collective will, guided by the Party, and
centered absolutely on the Leader, the society functions as a single, invincible living organism.

AN INTERNATIONAL
BANNER OF INDEPENDENCE
Juche positions itself as the
inevitable philosophical
evolution for the "Age of
Independence." It claims
universality not by demanding
other nations copy its exact
policies, but by insisting
that all nations must reject
subjugation, formulate
policies based on their unique
realities, and establish
complete sovereignty.
"Independence is the life and soul
for every country and people...
there should be neither
superior-subordinate relations nor
master-servant relations."
